title: GEM miner: a pipeline for mining engine version state and migration events in game repositories
description:
The pipeline that builds GEM (Game Engine Migration). It reads the engine version out of a tracked project file at every commit that touched it, rather than inferring migrations from commit messages: of the 97 Godot 3-to-4 boundary commits in the history tier, 19 name neither the engine nor a version in the subject line.

Stages, each a separate make target: the engine release timeline, the corpus frame, version snapshots, tier selection, instrument validation, per-commit history mining, issue-tracker demand collection, and the derivations. The version-extraction rule sits behind an adapter interface (miner/engines.py), so a second engine costs an adapter and a release timeline rather than a schema change; Unity and Unreal are declared alongside Godot, and only Godot is instantiated here.

make selftest runs offline with no credentials: adapter fixtures, the version-ordering trap, and a reproduction check confirming that the derived tables re-derive bit-for-bit at the release's own observation date.

Licensing. This record is the source code, under Apache-2.0. The repository archived here also carries the GEM v0.1 dataset under CC-BY-4.0 (see dataset/LICENSE), which is deposited separately as a dataset record; the related identifier below points to it.
notes: Git LFS is deliberately not used: Zenodo's GitHub integration archives the source zip without resolving LFS objects, which in the v0.1 release deposited the 39,553-row corpus frame as a 133-byte pointer. v0.1.1 corrects that; every table is a plain git object.
